verdict: Boeing's revenue rose 4% to $24.2B and its operations swung to a $354M profit, but $573M of interest expense left a $116M net loss — still a dramatic improvement from the $5.3B loss a year ago.

kpis.label: Operating earnings
kpis.note: Vs a $4.8B operating loss a year ago

kpis.label: Total backlog
kpis.note: A record; 161 jets delivered in the quarter

segments.name: Commercial Airplanes
segments.note: 161 deliveries (about flat) with a less favorable mix; the segment lost $697M as 777X and production-rate costs bit. The 737 program is progressing toward a stabilized 47/month rate.

segments.name: Defense, Space & Security
segments.note: Fighters, satellites, missiles and space — revenue up 15% on higher volume, with operating earnings of $492M.

segments.name: Global Services
segments.note: Parts, maintenance and training for airlines and militaries — the steadiest business, with an 18.3% operating margin. Shown after $41M of corporate eliminations.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — down from $1,522M a year ago.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: New aircraft and defense programs, net of customer funding.

otherDetail: Interest and debt expense of $573M, partly offset by $96M of other income (mostly pension-related credits).

takeaways.title: Operations back in profit
takeaways.text: A year ago operations lost $4.8B on a huge 777X charge. This quarter all three businesses contributed, led by services ($1,019M of earnings) and defense ($492M).

takeaways.title: Interest is the drag
takeaways.text: Debt taken on through the crisis years cost $573M of interest in one quarter — more than the operating profit — leaving a $116M net loss.

takeaways.title: Record backlog of $745B
takeaways.text: Orders grew to a record, including over 5,900 commercial jets — years of work, if Boeing can build them on schedule.

footerNote: Boeing counts $215M of income from operating investments inside its operating result; here it is netted against cost of revenue so the flow balances. Net loss attributable to Boeing common shareholders was $203M (the $0.26 loss per share) after $87M of dividends on mandatory convertible preferred stock; the chart shows the $116M consolidated net loss before those dividends.
